notes: 1. CP (Channel Partner / Growth Partner) portal login URL is the BARE root https://uat-web.xrportal.in/ which redirects to /login when unauthenticated; on success it lands on /dashboard. Role ID 3 (Channel Partner) is required for access (BRD §2, CP-FRD §7).

2. CP auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). Step 1 = mobile entry (+91 prefix, 'Enter Mobile Number'), Step 2 = 6-box OTP entry with a ~60s countdown + Re-Send OTP. The page heading is 'Growth Partner Login' (h2). JWT + user + permission state are stored in localStorage.

3. CP master/static OTP = 147258 (this is the CP/Buyer portal OTP per CLAUDE.md). It is NOT 258369 — that value is the Admin/SM ADMIN_MASTER_OTP and is rejected on the CP portal. UAT CP mobile = 8888888888 (lands directly on /dashboard).

4. POST-OTP BRANCHING (source-confirmed, Public/Login/index.jsx handleSubmit lines 222–259): after verify-otp 200 the FE inspects the user object — (a) isConsented===true && isCpRegistrationCompleted===true → navigate('/dashboard'); (b) !isConsented (false/null) → Undertaking modal; (c) isConsented===true && !isCpRegistrationCompleted → RegisterCp (Growth Partner Registration) modal. URL stays at '/' for both modals (antd overlays, NOT route changes).

5. INCOMPLETE/CONSENT FLOW FIXTURE: mobile 9999999991 + OTP 147258 reaches the Undertaking and RegisterCp modals (8888888888 lands straight on /dashboard and cannot reach them). 9999999991 is a STATEFUL UAT account — after a successful RegisterCp Submit the account flips to isCpRegistrationCompleted=true and is no longer reusable for this state. TCs MUST either navigate the modals WITHOUT submitting, or the team re-provisions between full runs. Do NOT save this session to channel-partner.json (reserved filename: channel-partner-incomplete.json). See CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline rule 7 (no live-portal mutations without user OK).

6. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT account/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. an unregistered CP mobile, a Buyer-role / SM-role mobile, an isActive=false CP, a soft-deleted CP, an aged/short-expiry JWT, a valid API bearer token / API client, or DB / audit-log read access).
7. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

8. SECURITY GAPS (documented — CP shares the SM/Admin auth.controller backend): No backend OTP rate limit / cooldown — the ~60s re-send gate is UI-only (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 3 is FE-only; backend throttle commented out). No wrong-OTP lockout. Logout is a client-side localStorage clear only — the JWT stays valid server-side until natural expiry (do NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case). isActive=false revoke blocks NEW send-otp but does NOT invalidate already-issued JWTs (CP_LGN_031 documents this as a bug). POST /cp/registration (RegisterCp submit) is UNAUTHENTICATED (BRD §9 ⚠, cp.routes.js). OTP generated with Math.random() and stored plaintext on users.otp. Master OTP has no production gate.

9. NOTIFICATION CHANNEL: OTP is delivered via Epinet SMS (NOT Kaleyra/WhatsApp) — CP-FS §1.7 + BRD §9 (FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25, communication.service.js). Kaleyra/Botspice WhatsApp is used for CUSTOMER registration notices, never for the CP's own login OTP. OTP verification itself dispatches NO SMS/WhatsApp/email (silent by design).

10. DOC_DRIFT-001 — CP-FS-Login (§URL) and CP-BRD §5 state the login URL as 'https://uat.xrportal.in/login'. LIVE (visual-memory cp/login INDEX.md + CLAUDE.md portal table) the CP portal is served at 'https://uat-web.xrportal.in/' (redirects to /login). The host 'uat.xrportal.in' is the BUYER portal. Live wins — every TC in this pass uses https://uat-web.xrportal.in/. BRD/FRD should be corrected to the uat-web host.

11. DOC_DRIFT-002 — CP-FRD-CP-Portal §9 lists 'Kaleyra | SMS/WhatsApp notifications' and CP-FS §1.4 says Send OTP 'Triggers OTP via SMS/WhatsApp'. The corrected source (CP-FS §1.7, BRD §9, FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25) is Epinet SMS for OTP — NOT WhatsApp, NOT Kaleyra. Live/corrected wins — TCs assert OTP via Epinet SMS only.

12. DOC_DRIFT-003 — CP-FS-Login §1.6 documents only 'profile complete → /dashboard' and 'profile incomplete → profile completion screen' (2 outcomes). LIVE (visual-memory, source-confirmed) there are THREE outcomes including a distinct 'Undertaking' consent modal (verify-otp isConsented=false) that precedes the RegisterCp modal. Live wins — the Undertaking modal is covered as its own sub-module.

13. GLOSSARY: 'Send OTP' = green full-width button on Step 1; 'Submit OTP' = green button on the OTP screen; 'Re-Send OTP' = inline link (button.common-link) on the OTP screen, disabled while the countdown runs; Back = the chevron-left back-icon on the OTP screen. 'Undertaking' = h4 consent modal with a single checkbox + 'I Disagree' / 'I Agree' (I Agree disabled until ticked). 'Growth Partner Registration' = the RegisterCp KYC/profile modal (h4) with PAN/GST/MAHA RERA uploads + Cancel/Submit. Invalid-OTP feedback is a transient Toastify toast (auto-dismisses fast).

tcs.scenario: To verify Send OTP with an unregistered mobile

tcs.scenario: To verify an unregistered mobile is rejected at Send OTP

tcs.scenario: To verify a concurrent Send OTP overwrites the stored OTP
tcs.description: Verify that issuing a second OTP for the same mobile overwrites the first (only the latest OTP is valid).
tcs.precond: Send OTP has been requested once for 8888888888. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to capture/observe two issued OTPs.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888' (OTP #1).
2. Re-Send OTP (after timer) for the same mobile (OTP #2).
3. Attempt to verify with OTP #1.
tcs.expected: The second send overwrites users.otp, so OTP #1 is no longer valid and only the latest OTP #2 verifies. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the overwrite behaviour and that the prior OTP is invalidated on re-issue.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Dashboard loads after successful login
tcs.description: Verify that a successful login lands on the CP Home Dashboard with its widgets.
tcs.precond: Successful OTP verification with 8888888888 / 147258.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete the OTP login flow.
2. Observe the landing page.
tcs.expected: The browser navigates to /dashboard and the Home Dashboard renders with stats cards, the referral widget, the 'Create New Lead' action and the Customers table (Source: visual-memory cp/login login-success-dashboard.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify the full mobile-to-dashboard login journey
tcs.description: Verify the complete CP login journey end-to-end: mobile, OTP, JWT storage, redirect to /dashboard.
tcs.precond: UAT; mobile 8888888888 registered as an active, consented, registration-complete CP.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/.
2. Type '8888888888'.
3. Click Send OTP.
4. On the OTP screen type '147258'.
5. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: verify-otp returns 200 with a JWT + user JSON; localStorage is populated with AUTH_TOKEN, user, permission_check, persist:xanadu_0.0.1 and is_jbp_submitted; the browser navigates from /login to /dashboard and the Home Dashboard renders.

tcs.scenario: To verify the master/static OTP bypasses validation
tcs.description: Verify the documented fact that the CP static/master OTP (147258) verifies for a valid CP mobile.
tcs.precond: The master OTP (147258) is configured; the OTP screen is shown for 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888'.
2. Enter '147258'.
3. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: Verification succeeds using the CP static/master OTP 147258 (bypasses real SMS delivery), works in all environments and issues a JWT. Note: this is the CP/Buyer OTP, NOT the Admin/SM 258369 (security gap — no production gate, note 8).

tcs.scenario: To verify verify-OTP returns the role permissions map
tcs.description: Verify that a successful verify-otp response carries the permission map used to gate the CP UI.
tcs.precond: A successful CP OTP verification has been performed. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DevTools / API visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a successful verify-otp for 8888888888.
2. Inspect the response body and localStorage 'permission_check'.
tcs.expected: The verify-otp response includes the user object and a permission matrix; the FE stores it as localStorage 'permission_check' ({moduleId: [permission ids]}) per visual-memory. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact module/action ids returned for role 3 (CP).

tcs.scenario: To verify the encryptedHvCode backfill on verify-otp
tcs.description: Verify the documented behaviour that verify-otp backfills the CP's encryptedHvCode where missing.
tcs.precond: A CP whose encryptedHvCode is not yet set. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP record missing encryptedHvCode + DB/API visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Send + verify OTP for a CP missing encryptedHvCode.
2. Inspect the user record / response for encryptedHvCode.
tcs.expected: On verify-otp the backend backfills/derives encryptedHvCode for the CP (referral hvCode used for walkInSourceXrCode per BRD §8). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the backfill is part of the CP verify path and not assumed.

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid OTP is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that submitting a wrong OTP shows an error and keeps the user on the OTP screen.
tcs.precond: Send OTP is complete for a valid CP mobile and the OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter an incorrect 6-digit OTP (e.g. '000000').
2. Click Submit OTP.
3. Observe the feedback.
tcs.expected: verify-otp returns 401; a transient Toastify error toast is shown briefly (auto-dismisses fast per visual-memory), no JWT is issued and there is no navigation to /dashboard.

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid OTP returns 401 and shows an error
tcs.description: Verify the invalid-OTP path: a wrong OTP fails verification with a 401 and a user-facing error.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown after sending OTP to 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '000000' into the six OTP boxes.
2. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: POST /api/v1/auth/cp/verify-otp returns 401 Unauthorized; a transient toast notification is shown and a console 'AxiosError: ... status code 401' is logged (visual-memory). No JWT is stored and the user stays on the OTP screen (or returns to mobile entry, timing-dependent).

tcs.scenario: To verify an OTP shorter than 6 digits is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a partial (less than 6-digit) OTP is blocked from submission.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '12345' (5 digits) into the OTP boxes.
2. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A validation message ('OTP must be 6 digits' / similar) is shown or Submit stays blocked; no verify-otp API call is fired and the user stays on the OTP screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit OTP is blocked when the OTP is incomplete
tcs.description: Verify that submitting with fewer than 6 OTP digits is blocked with a validation message.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter only 3 digits.
2. Click Submit OTP.
3. Then clear and leave all boxes empty and click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: Submit OTP is blocked (disabled or validation message 'OTP is required' / 'OTP must be 6 digits'); no verify API call is fired for the incomplete/empty OTP.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired OTP is rejected at Verify
tcs.description: Verify that submitting an OTP after the expiry window is rejected and the user is prompted to request a fresh one.
tcs.precond: Send OTP is complete and the OTP expiry window (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 2) is known.
tcs.steps:
1. Receive a valid OTP.
2. Wait past the configured expiry window without verifying.
3. Enter the now-expired OTP.
4. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: The OTP is rejected as expired (error 'OTP has expired' / 'Please request a new one'), no JWT is issued and the user is prompted to request a fresh OTP. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact expiry window and the on-expiry message string.

tcs.scenario: To verify an OTP submitted after the countdown without re-sending is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that letting the countdown expire and then submitting the originally-issued OTP is rejected as expired.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen countdown has reached 0 and no Re-Send was clicked.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP.
2. Wait until the countdown reaches 0.
3. Enter the originally received OTP '147258'.
4. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] verify is rejected with an expired-OTP error (or the master OTP 147258 may still succeed since it bypasses real OTP storage). Confirm whether the static/master OTP path is subject to the expiry window or always verifies (CP_LGN_032).

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no rate-limit / lockout on wrong OTP attempts
tcs.description: Verify the documented security gap that repeated wrong OTP attempts never lock the account or rate-limit, and a later correct OTP still succeeds.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown for 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit '111111'.
2. Submit '222222'.
3. Submit '333333'.
4. Submit several more random 6-digit OTPs.
5. Submit '147258'.
tcs.expected: Every wrong attempt is rejected (401) with no lockout and no rate-limit, and the final correct OTP '147258' succeeds and logs in. Document the security gap (note 8); the ~60s re-send gate is UI-only and no backend throttle is wired to the CP auth routes.

tcs.scenario: To verify a verify-otp 5xx surfaces a user-facing error
tcs.description: Verify that a server failure on verify-otp shows a friendly error and lets the user retry without reloading.
tcs.precond: The OTP screen is shown; a 500 can be simulated on the verify endpoint. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to force a 5xx (DevTools block/throttle).
tcs.steps:
1. Enter the OTP.
2. Force POST /api/v1/auth/cp/verify-otp to return a 500.
3. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: A user-friendly error such as 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' is shown (transient toast), any spinner clears and the user can retry without a page reload. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact 5xx error string surfaced on the CP screen.

tcs.scenario: To verify the verify-OTP 'Consent Pending' branch opens the Undertaking modal
tcs.description: Verify that a verify-otp for a CP whose isConsented is not yet set opens the Undertaking consent modal (no isConsented in the user body).
tcs.precond: CP mobile 9999999991 has isConsented=false/null. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture 9999999991 (do not submit — stateful, note 5).
tcs.steps:
1. Enter '9999999991'.
2. Send OTP, enter '147258', Submit OTP.
3. Observe the screen.
tcs.expected: verify-otp returns 'Consent Pending' with user.isConsented=false; the FE opens the 'Undertaking' modal (h4 'Undertaking', sub-heading 'Please read this agreement carefully before you proceed') as an antd overlay; the URL stays at '/'. (Source: visual-memory login-undertaking-modal.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the verify-OTP 'Consent Declined' branch (isConsented=false)
tcs.description: Verify that clicking 'I Disagree' on the Undertaking modal rejects the flow and returns to mobile entry.
tcs.precond: The Undertaking modal is shown for 9999999991. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the Undertaking modal.
2. Click 'I Disagree'.
3. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: handleConsent(false) fires: a toast 'You must accept the undertaking to proceed' is shown and the view resets to the mobile-entry screen; no JWT is issued and the dashboard does not load. (Source: visual-memory Undertaking modal note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Undertaking modal contents and controls
tcs.description: Verify that every element of the Undertaking modal is present per visual-memory (heading, agreement text, Read more, checkbox, two buttons).
tcs.precond: The Undertaking modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture 9999999991.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the Undertaking modal.
2. Read the heading and sub-heading.
3. Note the agreement text and the 'Read more' expander.
4. Note the consent checkbox and the two footer buttons.
tcs.expected: The modal shows h4 'Undertaking', h6 'Please read this agreement carefully before you proceed', scrollable agreement text starting 'The Vendor: (i) acknowledges that House of Abhinandan Lodha Private Limited...' with a 'Read more' expander, a single consent checkbox, and footer buttons 'I Disagree' (outline) and 'I Agree' (solid). No close button; keyboard-disabled. (Source: visual-memory login-undertaking-modal.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify 'I Agree' is disabled until the consent checkbox is ticked
tcs.description: Verify that the 'I Agree' button is disabled on modal open and enables only after the checkbox is ticked.
tcs.precond: The Undertaking modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the Undertaking modal (do not tick the checkbox).
2. Look at the 'I Agree' button state.
3. Tick the consent checkbox.
4. Look at the 'I Agree' button state again.
tcs.expected: On open 'I Agree' is disabled; after the consent checkbox is ticked 'I Agree' becomes enabled. A TC must assert toBeDisabled() BEFORE ticking the checkbox. (Source: visual-memory Undertaking modal note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Undertaking 'Read more' expander toggles
tcs.description: Verify that the inline 'Read more' expander in the agreement text expands and collapses the full text.
tcs.precond: The Undertaking modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the Undertaking modal.
2. Click 'Read more' in the agreement text.
3. Click it again ('Read less').
tcs.expected: Clicking 'Read more' expands the full agreement text and the link toggles to 'Read less'; clicking again collapses it. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the exact toggle label 'Read less' is inferred from visual-memory; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify 'I Agree' re-issues verify-otp with isConsented=1
tcs.description: Verify that ticking the checkbox and clicking 'I Agree' records consent and advances the flow.
tcs.precond: The Undertaking modal is shown for 9999999991; checkbox ticked. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-pending fixture (do NOT submit the subsequent RegisterCp form — stateful, note 5).
tcs.steps:
1. Tick the consent checkbox.
2. Click 'I Agree'.
3. Observe the next screen.
tcs.expected: handleConsent(true) re-issues verify-otp with isConsented=1; the response is 'Registration Pending' (isConsented=true, isCpRegistrationCompleted=null) and the FE then opens the 'Growth Partner Registration' (RegisterCp) modal. (Source: visual-memory — second verify-otp call.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the verify-OTP 'Registration Pending' branch opens RegisterCp
tcs.description: Verify that a CP who is consented but has not completed registration is shown the Growth Partner Registration (RegisterCp) modal.
tcs.precond: CP is consented (isConsented=true) but isCpRegistrationCompleted is not true. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] consent-done / registration-pending fixture (9999999991 after consenting).
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the consented state (via the Undertaking modal or a pre-consented account).
2. Observe the screen.
tcs.expected: verify-otp returns 'Registration Pending' (isConsented=true, isCpRegistrationCompleted=null); the FE opens the 'GROWTH PARTNER REGISTRATION' modal (h4) as an antd overlay; the URL stays at '/'. (Source: visual-memory login-incomplete-profile.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify an incomplete profile redirects to the RegisterCp screen
tcs.description: Verify that an incomplete-profile CP is routed to the RegisterCp profile-completion modal rather than the dashboard.
tcs.precond: A CP with isCpRegistrationCompleted not true. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture 9999999991.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in with the incomplete-profile CP mobile + OTP.
2. Observe the post-verify screen.
tcs.expected: After consent the CP is presented with the RegisterCp 'Growth Partner Registration' modal (profile completion), NOT the dashboard, per CP-FS §1.5 Rule 4 / CP-FRD §7.

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful OTP for an incomplete profile lands on RegisterCp (not /dashboard)
tcs.description: Verify the business rule that a valid OTP for an incomplete-profile CP routes to profile completion instead of the dashboard.
tcs.precond: Incomplete-profile CP fixture. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] 9999999991.
tcs.steps:
1. Send + verify OTP for the incomplete-profile CP.
2. Read the URL and the rendered screen.
tcs.expected: The URL stays at '/' (no /dashboard navigation) and the 'Growth Partner Registration' modal is shown for profile completion (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify the RegisterCp modal renders the mandatory KYC/profile fields
tcs.description: Verify that the Growth Partner Registration modal shows all documented sections and fields per visual-memory.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture (do NOT submit — stateful, note 5).
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Note the section headers and every field.
tcs.expected: The modal shows h4 'GROWTH PARTNER REGISTRATION' with sections 'Growth Partner Details', 'Additional Details', 'KYC Details' and the fields: phone (pre-filled/read-only), email*, ownerName*, orgName*, address*, Business Region* (select), phone2, email2, officePincode*, panNumber*, reraNumber, plus 3 upload slots (PAN Card / GST / MAHA RERA Certificate) and Cancel + Submit. (Source: visual-memory login-incomplete-profile.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify submitting an incomplete profile shows inline validation errors
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Submit with required RegisterCp fields empty blocks submission with field-level errors.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture (capture-only — do not complete a valid submit, note 5).
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Leave required fields (email, ownerName, orgName, address, Business Region, officePincode, panNumber) empty.
3. Click Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is blocked; Yup validation shows inline 'required' errors against each empty mandatory field (email, ownerName, orgName, address, Business Region, officePincode, panNumber). No registration is created.

tcs.scenario: To verify the RegisterCp phone field is pre-filled and read-only
tcs.description: Verify that the phone field in the RegisterCp modal is pre-populated from login and not editable.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown for 9999999991. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Look at the phone field value.
3. Try to edit it.
tcs.expected: The phone field is pre-filled with the logged-in mobile (9999999991) and appears read-only/disabled — it cannot be edited. (Source: visual-memory RegisterCp field table.)

tcs.scenario: To verify RegisterCp field-format validation (email / PAN / pincode)
tcs.description: Verify that the RegisterCp form enforces format validation on email, PAN and pincode before allowing submit.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture (capture-only).
tcs.steps:
1. Enter an invalid email ('abc@'), an invalid PAN ('12345'), and a non-numeric pincode in their fields.
2. Attempt to Submit.
tcs.expected: Field-level format errors are shown (email must be valid; ownerName must match the name regex; PAN/pincode format). Submit is blocked until the formats are valid. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact PAN/pincode regex enforced by Yup.

tcs.scenario: To verify the RegisterCp document uploads accept type/size limits
tcs.description: Verify that the PAN / GST / MAHA RERA upload slots enforce the documented format and size limits.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture + sample files (valid PDF/JPG/PNG <=2MB and an oversize/invalid-type file).
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Upload a valid PDF/JPG/PNG (<=2MB) to the PAN slot.
3. Try uploading a >2MB file and a disallowed type (e.g. .exe) to the GST slot.
tcs.expected: Valid PDF/JPG/PNG files up to 2MB are accepted; oversize or disallowed-type files are rejected with a validation message. (Source: visual-memory RegisterCp upload notes — PDF/JPG/PNG, <=2MB.) [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact reject message and size cap.

tcs.scenario: To verify Cancel on the RegisterCp modal resets to mobile entry
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Cancel on the RegisterCp modal aborts registration and returns to the mobile-entry screen.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Click Cancel.
3. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: handleRegisterationCancel fires: a toast 'You must register to proceed' is shown and the view resets to the mobile-entry screen; no registration is created and the dashboard does not load. (Source: visual-memory RegisterCp note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify completing the profile redirects to the Dashboard
tcs.description: Verify that a successful RegisterCp submit completes registration and lands the CP on the dashboard.
tcs.precond: A disposable incomplete-profile CP account is provisioned for a one-time submit. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a DISPOSABLE registration-pending CP — a valid Submit is a live mutation (note 5 / CLAUDE.md rule 7) and flips the account to isCpRegistrationCompleted=true. Requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal on a disposable account.
2. Fill all required fields with valid data and the 3 uploads.
3. Click Submit (only with authorisation).
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP + valid profile data + sample docs
tcs.expected: expressPostFormData(apiUrls.cpRegister, ...) succeeds; the FE stores AUTH_TOKEN, user and is_jbp_submitted, shows a success animation (Lottie) and navigates to /dashboard. (Source: visual-memory RegisterCp Submit note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful profile submit issues a JWT and redirects
tcs.description: Verify that the RegisterCp submit response issues a JWT and the CP is authenticated on the dashboard.
tcs.precond: A disposable incomplete-profile CP account. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP — live mutation, requires authorisation (note 5).
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a valid RegisterCp submit on a disposable account.
2. Inspect localStorage and the landing page.
tcs.expected: A JWT (AUTH_TOKEN) is stored along with the user object and is_jbp_submitted; the CP is authenticated and lands on /dashboard. The session must NOT be saved to channel-partner.json (reserved: channel-partner-incomplete.json, note 5).

tcs.scenario: To verify a reload during profile completion keeps the CP on RegisterCp
tcs.description: Verify that refreshing while the RegisterCp modal is open re-routes the still-incomplete CP back to RegisterCp, not the dashboard.
tcs.precond: The RegisterCp modal is shown for an incomplete-profile CP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. Reach the RegisterCp modal.
2. Hard refresh (F5).
3. Observe the screen.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] On reload the still-incomplete CP is re-evaluated; expected to be returned to the RegisterCp profile-completion modal (not /dashboard) because isCpRegistrationCompleted is still not true. Confirm whether the session survives reload at this stage or the CP must re-authenticate.

tcs.scenario: To verify direct /dashboard access by an incomplete-profile CP redirects to RegisterCp
tcs.description: Verify that an incomplete-profile CP who navigates directly to /dashboard is routed to profile completion.
tcs.precond: An incomplete-profile CP session exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] incomplete-profile fixture.
tcs.steps:
1. As an incomplete-profile CP, navigate directly to /dashboard.
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the incomplete-profile CP is redirected to the RegisterCp profile-completion screen rather than seeing the dashboard (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 4). Confirm the guard fires on a direct /dashboard hit.

tcs.scenario: To verify a Buyer-role mobile cannot log in on the CP login page
tcs.description: Verify that a Buyer (role 2) mobile is rejected on the CP login page per CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6.
tcs.precond: A Buyer-role-only mobile is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Buyer-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. On the CP login page enter the Buyer-role mobile.
2. Send OTP (and, if it advances, verify).
tcs.expected: The Buyer (role 2) is rejected on the CP login — the CP lookup is scoped to role 3; send-otp or verify returns an error and login does not proceed (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6).

tcs.scenario: To verify Buyer credentials do not work on CP login
tcs.description: Verify cross-role rejection — a Buyer (role 2) cannot authenticate via the CP login page end-to-end.
tcs.precond: On the CP login page. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Buyer-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /login.
2. Enter the Buyer-role mobile.
3. Send OTP, enter an OTP and Submit.
tcs.expected: Per CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6 the Buyer role cannot use the CP login page; the flow is rejected and the user stays on the CP login screen with no JWT issued.

tcs.scenario: To verify an SM-role mobile cannot log in on the CP login page
tcs.description: Verify that an SM (role 4/5) mobile is rejected on the CP login page per CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6.
tcs.precond: An SM-role-only mobile is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. On the CP login page enter the SM-role mobile.
2. Send OTP (and, if it advances, verify).
tcs.expected: The SM (role 4/5) is rejected on the CP login — the CP lookup is scoped to role 3; login does not proceed (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6).

tcs.scenario: To verify SM credentials do not work on CP login
tcs.description: Verify cross-role rejection — an SM (role 4/5) cannot authenticate via the CP login page end-to-end.
tcs.precond: On the CP login page. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM-role mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /login.
2. Enter the SM-role mobile.
3. Send OTP, enter an OTP and Submit.
tcs.expected: Per CP-FS §1.5 Rule 6 the SM role cannot use the CP login page; the flow is rejected and no JWT is issued.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Admin/SM OTP (258369) is rejected on the CP portal
tcs.description: Verify OTP portal-isolation — the Admin/SM master OTP does not verify on the CP portal.
tcs.precond: On the CP OTP screen for 8888888888.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for '8888888888' on the CP portal.
2. Enter the Admin/SM OTP '258369'.
3. Click Submit OTP.
tcs.expected: verify-otp rejects the OTP (401) — only the CP static OTP 147258 succeeds on this portal; an error toast is shown, no JWT is issued and there is no navigation. (OTP is portal-specific per CLAUDE.md; 258369 is Admin/SM only.)

tcs.scenario: To verify auth state is stored in localStorage
tcs.description: Verify that the CP auth state is persisted in localStorage (not sessionStorage / not cookies for the token).
tcs.precond: About to perform a successful CP login.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools > Application > Storage.
2. Complete a successful login (8888888888 / 147258).
3. Inspect localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies.
tcs.expected: localStorage holds AUTH_TOKEN (JWT), user, permission_check, persist:xanadu_0.0.1 and is_jbp_submitted; the token is in localStorage (not sessionStorage). (Source: visual-memory Auth Mechanism note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the JWT session persists across a page refresh
tcs.description: Verify that refreshing after login keeps the CP authenticated on the dashboard.
tcs.precond: A successful CP login has completed; on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Refresh the page (F5).
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: AUTH_TOKEN and persist:xanadu_0.0.1 persist; the CP stays on /dashboard (not redirected to /login) and the Home Dashboard re-renders.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists across a page reload
tcs.description: Verify the session survives a reload while the JWT is unexpired.
tcs.precond: Logged in as CP on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Hard refresh /dashboard.
2. Confirm no login prompt appears.
tcs.expected: The CP remains authenticated on /dashboard after reload (JWT restored from localStorage); no login prompt is shown.

tcs.scenario: To verify an authenticated CP navigating to /login redirects to /dashboard
tcs.description: Verify that an already-authenticated CP who opens /login is bounced to /dashboard.
tcs.precond: Logged in as CP with a valid JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. While logged in, navigate to /login.
2. Observe the redirect.
tcs.expected: The app detects the active session and redirects /login → /dashboard; the login form is not shown to an authenticated CP.

tcs.scenario: To verify the session persists in a new tab
tcs.description: Verify that opening /dashboard in a new tab of the same browser does not prompt for login.
tcs.precond: The CP is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new tab in the same browser.
2. Go to /dashboard.
tcs.expected: The new tab loads /dashboard directly without a login prompt (the JWT is shared via localStorage).

tcs.scenario: To verify direct /dashboard access while logged out redirects to /login
tcs.description: Verify that navigating to /dashboard with no session redirects to the CP login.
tcs.precond: No CP session in the browser (localStorage cleared).
tcs.steps:
1. Open a browser without a CP JWT.
2. Navigate directly to /dashboard.
3. Observe the redirect.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to /login; the dashboard is not loaded and no protected data is exposed.

tcs.scenario: To verify the auth gate on unauthenticated protected-route access
tcs.description: Verify that a direct deep-link to a protected CP route in a fresh session redirects to /login.
tcs.precond: localStorage cleared / no AUTH_TOKEN.
tcs.steps:
1. Open a new incognito window.
2. Navigate directly to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/dashboard.
tcs.expected: The app detects the missing JWT and redirects to /login; the CP login page renders and no protected data is shown.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired JWT returns 401 'Your session has expired'
tcs.description: Verify that an expired CP JWT is rejected with a 401 and a session-expired message.
tcs.precond: An expired CP JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an aged/expired JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Place an expired JWT in localStorage.
2. Reload /dashboard / call a protected endpoint.
tcs.expected: The protected request fails with 401 and a 'Your session has expired' message; the user is redirected to /login. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact 401 message string.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired JWT redirects a protected route to /login
tcs.description: Verify the routing effect of an expired JWT — the protected route bounces to login.
tcs.precond: An expired CP JWT is in storage. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an expired JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. With an expired JWT present, navigate to /dashboard.
2. Observe the redirect.
tcs.expected: The expired token fails validation and the CP is redirected to /login; no protected data renders.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered JWT forces a redirect to /login
tcs.description: Verify that editing the stored JWT causes the protected request to fail and the CP to be sent to login.
tcs.precond: The CP is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools > Application > localStorage.
2. Change a character in the stored AUTH_TOKEN.
3. Reload /dashboard.
tcs.expected: The protected API call fails with 401 and the CP is redirected to /login. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm a tampered-signature token is rejected (not silently accepted).

tcs.scenario: To verify the session survives a browser restart within the JWT window
tcs.description: Verify that closing and reopening the browser within the JWT validity window keeps the CP logged in.
tcs.precond: The CP is logged in and the JWT is stored in localStorage.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in successfully.
2. Close the browser completely.
3. Reopen and go to /dashboard.
tcs.expected: The session is restored from localStorage and /dashboard loads without redirecting to login (JWT validity ~24h / 86400s per visual-memory JWT note). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the CP JWT lifetime; BRD does not state the exact window.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout clears localStorage and redirects to /login
tcs.description: Verify that logging out clears the client auth state and returns the CP to the login page.
tcs.precond: The CP is logged in; on /dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Logout in the user menu.
2. Observe the redirect.
3. Inspect localStorage.
4. Try navigating back to /dashboard.
tcs.expected: AUTH_TOKEN, user, permission_check, persist:xanadu_0.0.1 and is_jbp_submitted are removed from localStorage; the CP is redirected to /login; revisiting /dashboard redirects back to /login.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout is a client-side clear only (JWT stays valid server-side)
tcs.description: Verify the documented security gap that the JWT remains usable after logout until natural expiry.
tcs.precond: The CP is logged in with an active JWT. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access to replay the captured JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Capture the JWT bearer token.
2. Click Logout (client-side clear / redirect to /login).
3. Immediately call a protected CP endpoint with the captured JWT.
tcs.expected: Logout clears the client session, but the captured JWT STILL succeeds on the protected endpoint — the token is stateless with no server-side blacklist, so it stays valid until its natural expiry. QA must NOT write a post-logout 401 pass case (security gap, note 8 — shared with Admin/SM auth.controller).

tcs.scenario: To verify verify-OTP issues a JWT only in the consented + registered terminal branch
tcs.description: Verify the documented branching — a JWT is returned only when the CP is consented AND registration-complete; the consent/registration-pending branches open modals instead.
tcs.precond: Three CP states are available: consented+complete (8888888888), consent-pending and registration-pending (9999999991). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] the three fixtures.
tcs.steps:
1. Verify OTP as 8888888888 (consented+complete).
2. Verify OTP as a consent-pending CP.
3. Verify OTP as a registration-pending CP.
4. Compare the responses/outcomes.
tcs.expected: Only the consented+registration-complete branch navigates to /dashboard with a JWT; the consent-pending branch opens the Undertaking modal and the registration-pending branch opens RegisterCp — neither lands on the dashboard with a usable session until consent + registration are complete (source-confirmed handleSubmit branching, note 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify the protect middleware accepts Authorization header OR jwt cookie
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that the protect middleware reads the token from either the Authorization header or a jwt cookie.
tcs.precond: A valid CP JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call a protected CP endpoint with the token in the Authorization: Bearer header.
2. Call the same endpoint with the token only in a 'jwt' cookie.
tcs.expected: Both calls are accepted — the protect middleware reads the token from the Authorization header OR a jwt cookie. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the dual-source token acceptance and whether the cookie path is intended (potential CSRF surface).

tcs.scenario: To verify the profile-submit endpoint is PUBLIC (no JWT required)
tcs.description: Verify the documented security gap that POST /cp/registration (RegisterCp submit) is unauthenticated.
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access; a disposable payload (do not create real records without authorisation).
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /cp/registration with a valid body and NO Authorization header.
2. Read the HTTP status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint accepts the request without a JWT — it is PUBLIC (BRD §9 ⚠ 'POST /cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED', cp.routes.js). Document the security gap; do not treat the unauthenticated acceptance as a pass to be 'fixed' silently — it is a known gap. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exposure and any rate/abuse controls.

tcs.scenario: To verify isActive=false revoke does NOT invalidate existing JWTs
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that revoking a CP (isActive=false) blocks new send-otp but leaves already-issued JWTs valid.
tcs.precond: A CP is logged in with an active JWT, then the admin sets isActive=false. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to flip isActive=false + the captured JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as the CP and capture the JWT.
2. Have the admin set the CP's isActive=false.
3. Re-attempt send-otp for the CP (expect revoked).
4. Call a protected endpoint with the previously captured JWT.
tcs.expected: send-otp is blocked with 'access revoked' (CP_LGN_030), but the previously-issued JWT STILL succeeds on the protected endpoint until its natural expiry — revoke does not invalidate live tokens (documented BUG, note 8). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm with the security team.

tcs.scenario: To verify SQL injection in the mobile field is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a SQL-injection string in the mobile field is blocked by the numeric-only input.
tcs.precond: The CP login page is loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Try entering "' OR 1=1 --" in the mobile field.
2. Click Send OTP.
tcs.expected: The input is blocked at field level (numeric only); no DB error occurs and no login happens.

tcs.scenario: To verify XSS injection in the mobile field is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a script payload in the mobile field is not executed.
tcs.precond: The CP login page is loaded.
tcs.steps: 1. Try entering '<script>alert(1)</script>' in the mobile field.
tcs.expected: The script tags are blocked by the numeric-only field; no JavaScript alert fires and no payload is reflected.

tcs.scenario: To verify auth requests are HTTPS only with no OTP in the URL
tcs.description: Verify that the login page and all CP auth requests use HTTPS and never carry mobile/OTP in the URL.
tcs.precond: DevTools is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Confirm the address bar shows https:// on the CP login.
2. Capture the send-otp and verify-otp requests in the Network tab.
3. Check the request method, URL and body.
tcs.expected: All auth requests are HTTPS; the mobile and OTP are sent in the request body, never in the URL/query; no mixed-content warnings and the auth payload is not logged to the console.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP is generated insecurely and stored in plaintext
tcs.description: Verify the documented gaps that CP OTPs are generated with Math.random() and persisted as plaintext.
tcs.precond: DB query access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for the CP user.
2. Query the users row for the otp / otpExpires columns.
tcs.expected: The otp column holds the literal 6-digit code in plaintext and is generated via Math.floor(100000 + Math.random()*900000) (not a CSPRNG). Document the gaps; recommend hashing (bcrypt/HMAC) and crypto.randomInt. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the CP path shares the Admin/SM generator.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OTP is delivered via Epinet SMS (not Kaleyra/WhatsApp)
tcs.description: Verify that the CP login OTP is dispatched through Epinet SMS and NOT Kaleyra/WhatsApp.
tcs.precond: Backend outbound network-log capture is available; a valid CP mobile. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for 8888888888.
2. Inspect the backend's outbound HTTP traffic.
tcs.expected: The outbound OTP hits the Epinet SMS endpoint; there is NO Kaleyra/WhatsApp call for the OTP (CP-FS §1.7, BRD §9, FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25). Kaleyra/Botspice is used only for CUSTOMER notifications, never the CP login OTP (see DOC_DRIFT-002, note 11).

tcs.scenario: To verify Epinet SMS dispatch is fire-and-forget
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that send-otp returns success even when the outbound SMS dispatch fails.
tcs.precond: Backend with a simulated outbound failure to Epinet. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] network-fault injection + DB visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Block outbound traffic to the Epinet endpoint.
2. Send OTP for the CP mobile.
3. Inspect the response and the users.otp row.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 200 'OTP sent successfully' even though no message left the system, and the user row still has otp/otpExpires set (send calls are not awaited — fire-and-forget). Document the gap. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the CP path shares this behaviour.

tcs.scenario: To verify OTP verification sends no notification
tcs.description: Verify that successfully verifying the OTP does NOT send any SMS, WhatsApp or email (silent by design).
tcs.precond: A CP successfully verifies the OTP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] message-log visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a successful OTP verification.
2. Check outbound message logs for SMS/WhatsApp/email tied to this verification.
tcs.expected: No SMS, WhatsApp or email is dispatched on OTP verification (silent by design — the only login notification channel is the Epinet OTP send). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no side-channel notification on verify.

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful login is recorded in the audit log
tcs.description: Verify that a successful CP login is recorded with timestamp, mobile and role per CP-FS §1.8.
tcs.precond: An active CP logs in successfully. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] audit-log read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current timestamp.
2. Complete CP login with 8888888888 / 147258.
3. Query the audit log for the latest LOGIN event.
tcs.expected: An audit-log row exists with the CP's user ID, role 3 (CP), mobile number and a timestamp within seconds of the login (CP-FS §1.8). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the audit table/columns.

tcs.scenario: To verify a failed login is recorded in the audit log
tcs.description: Verify that a failed CP login attempt is recorded in the audit log.
tcs.precond: A valid CP mobile is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] audit-log read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send OTP for the valid CP mobile.
2. Enter a wrong OTP '000000'.
3. Click Submit OTP.
4. Query the audit log.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] CP-FS §1.8 documents login-event logging but does not confirm failed-attempt logging. Confirm whether a failed-login audit entry is written (mobile, timestamp, failure reason).

tcs.scenario: To verify the CP send-otp endpoint accepts a valid CP mobile (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the CP send-otp API returns success for a registered CP mobile.
tcs.precond: An API client / valid environment is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /api/v1/auth/cp/send-otp with the CP mobile (+ countryCode '+91').
2. Read the HTTP status and response body.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with 'OTP sent successfully' (the response carries otpExpires). (Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/cp/send-otp per visual-memory API list.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the CP verify-otp endpoint returns a token and user (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the CP verify-otp API returns a JWT and user object for the correct mobile + OTP (consented + complete CP).
tcs.precond: An API client is available and send-otp has been called for 8888888888. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call POST /api/v1/auth/cp/verify-otp with phone, otp 147258, countryCode.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a JWT and a user object (isConsented=true, isCpRegistrationCompleted=true). (Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/cp/verify-otp.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the verify-otp permissions in the API response
tcs.description: Verify that a successful verify-otp response includes the permission map used to gate the CP UI.
tcs.precond: A successful CP verify-otp has been performed. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Perform a successful verify-otp for the CP mobile.
2. Inspect the response body for a permissions field.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the verify-otp response includes a permission structure stored as localStorage 'permission_check' ({moduleId: [permission ids]}). [To verify] confirm the exact module/action ids returned for role 3 (CP).

tcs.scenario: To verify injection at the API layer bypasses the field block
tcs.description: Verify backend handling when a SQLi/XSS payload is sent directly to the CP send-otp API (bypassing the numeric-only field).
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp with phone set to an injection payload.
2. Read the response and check for DB/error leakage.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the UI numeric-only block does not apply at the API. The backend should safely reject (parameterised queries; failing the user lookup with a 'User not found' / 4xx) with no SQL error and no script reflection. [To verify] confirm backend sanitisation.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no backend OTP cooldown (API)
tcs.description: Verify the documented gap that CP send-otp has no server-side rate limit — the ~60s re-send gate is UI-only.
tcs.precond: An API client is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call send-otp for the CP mobile.
2. Immediately call send-otp again, back-to-back, several times.
tcs.expected: Every back-to-back send-otp call succeeds — there is NO server-side cooldown (CP-FS §1.5 Rule 3 is UI-only). Document the gap; do not test backend cooldown as a passing case (note 8).
